item.title: ‘Engraved with initials’: Titanic passenger's gold pocket watch sold for 1.78m pounds; memorabilia auction sets new record
item.description: A gold pocket watch belonging to Titanic victim Isidor Straus, Macy's co-owner, fetched a record 1.78 million pounds at auction. The 18-karat timepiece, which stopped at the moment the ship sank, was gifted to him in 1888.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Europe seeks Nato-style pact, higher army cap for Ukraine
Troubled by US Venezuela operation, Europeans limit intel sharing
item.description: The US military operation against Venezuelan alleged drug traffickers coupled with threats by Donald Trump for a ground assault against President Nicolas Maduro have troubled European powers who retain strategically located territories in the Caribbean, observers say. Washington accuses Maduro of leading a "terrorist" drug cartel, a charge he denies.

item.title: A woman leads Japan, yet she’s still forbidden from entering sumo’s sacred ring
item.description: Japan’s first female prime minister, Sanae Takaichi, leads the nation yet remains barred from entering sumo’s sacred ring, prompting debate over the taboo against women in the dohyo. The rule is inconsistently applied, even as modern Japan questions its values, and Takaichi’s conservative stance complicates whether her historic leadership will challenge or uphold a tradition that has kept women outside the sport’s most sacred space.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Indian-origin 'cocaine lawyer' Deepak Paradkar arrested in Canada for helping ex-Olympian kill FBI witness
item.description: Canada's 'cocaine lawyer', Deepak Paradkar, faces extradition to the US for allegedly aiding Ryan Wedding, a former Olympian-turned-drug lord to kill an FBi witness. Paradkar helped Wedding in his day-to-day drug cartel operations, the US claimed in its indictment. The allegations are not yet proved.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Lakshmi Mittal leaves UK over 'inheritance tax', now a Swiss resident, claims report
item.description: A report claimed that Indian-origin steel tycoon Lakshmi Mittal have left the UK and relocated to Switzerland. The report claimed that UK's inheritance tax has driven Mittal out like many other super-rich as UK taxes them on earnings from assets in other countries and inheritance as well. Mittal has future plans to settle in Dubai, the report said.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 'We did not forget': Who is Nazeer Hameed, Indian man wanted in the US for 2017 murder of co-worker's wife and son?
item.description: A drop of blood in the crime scene led the investigators of the 2017 New Jersey mother-son murder to Nazeer Hameed, a coworker of the woman's husband. Nazeer already came to India and denied to give DNA samples. Investigators got a court order to request the Indian company where he was working to send them his office-issued laptop for the DNA match.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: No entry ever: Indian man visits Canada to see newborn grandchild, harasses teens; faces deportation
item.description: An Indian national, Jagjit Singh, visiting Canada on a temporary visa, has been convicted of criminally harassing two teenage girls near their school. Singh's actions, including attempting to take photos and putting his arm around a student, led to his arrest and a jail sentence following which he has been ordered to be deported and never to return to Canada.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Canada set to overhaul citizenship-by-descent rules; big relief for Indian-origin families
item.description: Canada's Citizenship Act is undergoing a significant overhaul with Bill C-3, poised to benefit thousands of Indian-origin families. This landmark legislation abolishes the "second-generation cut-off," restoring citizenship to those previously excluded and establishing a "substantial connection test" for future generations born abroad. The law, awaiting its effective date, promises greater fairness and inclusivity for Canadian families.
item.dc:creator: Lubna Kably

item.title: Flying this Thanksgiving? The TSA tips you’ll actually need as almost 18 million travellers hit the airports
item.description: Thanksgiving 2025 is shaping up to be one of the busiest travel weeks in years, with packed airports, crowded roads, and millions moving at once. Air travel leads the surge, backed by record TSA volumes and an intense flight schedule. With early planning, smart tools, and a flexible backup plan, travellers can still navigate the rush and reach home smoothly.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Mamdani says he will always call Trump a 'fascist' and 'despot', explains what changed after White House meeting
item.description: Zohran Mamdani addressed the 'fascist' question again Sunday after President Donald Trump saved him from a difficult situation. The question was whether Mamdani still considered Trump as a 'despot' even after their first meeting that appeared very cordial. Trump said he did not mind being called a despot as he had been called much worse. Mamdani asserted that he still considered Trump as a 'fascist' and all the negative things he said about him in past.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: FBI defends Kash Patel’s use of SWAT protection for girlfriend, saying she faced ‘hundreds of credible threats’
item.description: The FBI defends Director Kash Patel's decision to deploy SWAT agents for his girlfriend, Alexis Wilkins, citing hundreds of credible death threats. This action, along with his use of government jets for personal trips, faces criticism from officials and lawmakers for alleged misuse of resources and blurring personal and official boundaries.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 'As an Indian-American....': US diplomat who was posted in Chennai says H-1B is industrialized fraud
item.description: US diplomat Mahvash Siddiqui, who was posted in India 20 years ago and was dealing with H-1B visas, claimed that there is a industry in India which is running the H-1B fraud. Appearing on a podcast in her individual capacity, she said she is speaking out of her concerns for American youth and not as a diplomat. She said a myth has been created for years that America needs STEM workers from outside.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘To target supreme leader’: Iran warns of attempts to assassinate Khamenei; plot to destabilise country
item.description: Iran's intelligence ministry has warned of alleged foreign attempts, including by the US and Israel, to assassinate Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and destabilize the Islamic Republic. Intelligence Minister Esmail Khatib stated that "the enemy seeks to target the supreme leader," a rare direct accusation. These warnings come amid heightened tensions and past military actions between Iran and Israel.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Who is Lindsey Halligan? From Miss Colorado finalist to being called Trump’s ‘puppet’ to prosecute Comey
item.description: A former Miss Colorado USA finalist, Lindsey Halligan, now faces intense scrutiny as an interim US attorney appointed by Donald Trump. Her rapid rise and handling of the James Comey case have sparked controversy, including a public clash with the overseeing judge over alleged "puppet" remarks, raising questions about political motives and prosecutorial judgment.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 'It was uncomfortable for me': US F-16 pilot 'shocked' that Dubai air show went on even after Tejas crash
item.description: US F-16 pilot Captain Taylor Hiester expressed shock and discomfort as Dubai Air Show went on after a Tejas fighter jet crashed killing Wing Commander Namansh Syal. Hiester's team, along with others, cancelled their performances out of respect, but he said when he returned to the site after an hour, he saw the crowd enjoying the show and the announcer hosting the show with unabated enthusiasm.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Candace Owens drops explosive claim on Charlie Kirk's assassination with shocking twist about Tyler Robinson fingerprints
item.description: Candace Owens questions the official narrative surrounding Charlie Kirk's shooting, suggesting a planned setup involving multiple individuals. She claims Tyler Robinson's role was limited, with his fingerprints not being the only ones on the weapon. Owens also alleges Lance Twiggs played a more significant, albeit different, part in the incident, citing a TMZ video as evidence.
item.dc:creator: Sehjal Gupta

item.title: COLA increases Social Security payments for 2026: Boosts confirmed for retirees, spouses, survivors and disability recipients
item.description: Social Security beneficiaries will see a 2.8% increase in their monthly payments starting January 2026. This adjustment will benefit over 75 million Americans, including retirees and disabled workers. While welcome, the rise may not fully cover escalating living costs, especially healthcare. Higher earnings limits for those working while receiving benefits are also set for 2026.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Kash Patel's girlfriend shuts trolls with 3-word jibe; proves she is not from Israel
item.description: Kash Patel's girlfriend Alexis Wilkins turned X's new feature to show the location in her stride and came at her trolls who claim she is from Israel. Sharing the screenshot of her X account that shows the account was created in the US and is based in US, Wilkins called this the best feature of X.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Who is Indian-origin Nicholas Singh, one of Canada's 25 most wanted criminals, arrested in Toronto?
item.description: Canadian authorities apprehended Indian-origin Nicholas Singh, a high-risk fugitive, in Toronto. Singh, wanted for parole violations and previously convicted of robbery and firearm offenses, was found with a firearm and ammunition. He was at No 15 on Canada's list of 25 most wanted fugitives.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk
